newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki slips on weak results, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki slips on weak results, profit-taking.

text.p: Shares closed lower after lively Wednesday trade as results from food and feed maker Cultor and engineering group Metra came in below expectations and investors took profits in recently powerful Merita, brokers said.
The HEX index fell 0.89 percent to 2,200.23. Volume was a healthy 461 million markka.
Cultor fell 15.00 markka to close at 229.00 after reporting a 42 percent slide in its January-August earnings.
Metra closed down 7.00 markka at 269.00, despite slightly higher January-August profits.
"Merita was very much in focus," one broker said. The bank stock shed 0.50 markka to end at 12.30; and remained quite lively as some took profits from its recent strong gains.
Forestries tracked weakness in U.S. paper stocks, with the sub-index falling 1.67 percent.
UPM-Kymmene was down 1.00 markka to 95.40, Enso was off 1.20 at 35.60 and Metsa-Serla closed down 0.50 at 29.50.
Brokers said the slide in forestries was also fed by remarks from Sweden's Sodra suggesting the forest industry's long-awaited upturn was emerging slowly.
Telecom heavyweight Nokia fell 1.70 markka to 209.00, after a weaker opening on Wall Street. Nokia accounted for 25 percent of total bourse volume.
The market was expected to remain jittery amid rising pessimism ahead of more eight-month results from major listed companies -- particularly forestries -- this week and next.
"We might see some pretty bad results," one broker said.
